utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Ms. Mahindaratne, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The Prosecution calls Bosko Dzolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dzolic. Before you give evidence, the Rules require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. May I invite you to make that declaration of which the text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dzolic. Please be seated. It is Ms. Mahindaratne who will examine you first. Ms. Mahindaratne, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dzolic.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: My name is Bosko Dzolic. I am a retired officer of the Croatian army. I don't know if I need to give you any other details.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No that is not necessary, Mr. Dzolic. I'll ask you questions and you can just respond to the question. Were you interviewed by members of the Office of the Prosecutor on 17th and 18th May, 2004?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And was that interview conducted via an interpreter?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And in the course of that interview, when the investigators asked you questions, did you answer truthfully?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And was that statement recorded at that time, as in type written?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: It was type written, yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And at the completion of the interview, was that statement read back to you in your language?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And did you sign that statement as accurately reflecting what you had stated in the course of the interview?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I signed the statement, but it was in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will come to the next part. Then, on 20th August, Mr. Dzolic, did you meet with members of the Office of the Prosecutor at what was referred to as a proofing session?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you examine your previous statement in your language and provide certain changes to your previous statement?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And at that time, did you also provide further clarifications and additional information?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And in the course of that second interview, when questions were asked of you, did you answer truthfully --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I just raise a matter here. My learned friend has led the fact of clarifications and additional information. I have that second statement and read it and the Court has as well; and in my submission, the witness should not be led in relation to those changes, but should be asked for his opinion as to why he altered the first statement. Clarifications, modifications may hold, and additional information may hide a multitude of sins, and it is a statement of significance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that. Whether it is just clarifications, additional information, or corrections, changes, Ms. Mahindaratne, apparently Mr. Kay takes issue with that. At this moment -- Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would add to that, how a 36-paragraph supplemental statement could be called clarification is beyond me as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kuzmanovic, I said how to qualify this. I was just about to say that. Apparently, the characterization of the proofing session statement seems to divide the parties. Ms. Mahindaratne, Mr. Kay, Mr. Kuzmanovic, I think at this moment what we're doing is seeking - not the Bench but apparently you, Ms. Mahindaratne - you're seeking to find a way to admission of these documents in which, as a matter of fact, the whys are not at this moment of primarily importance. So let's not quarrel at this moment how to qualify them. Of course, further exploring the reasons and the characterization can take place during the examination-in-chief and the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In order to save time, Mr. President, I will use a neutral term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, then, for the time being and for what the purposes we are doing at this moment, that would do; and then, at a later stage perhaps, we can further explore the other matters. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, on 20th August 2008, did you provide a supplementary statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: On -- on the 20th of August, 2008, did you provide a second statement to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, now, at the completion of that interview -- you have problems. You indicated you had problems hearing. Can you hear me, Mr. Dzolic?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I can hear you, but there's something interrupting the sound. Now it's all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Is it all right?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, on that occasion, when you were asked questions by the -- I'm referring to the second occasion, 20th August 2008, when you were asked questions by the members of the Office of the Prosecutor, did you answer them truthfully?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, to the best of your knowledge, Mr. Dzolic, are the contents of your two statements - that is, the one provided by you on 17th and 18th May 2004 and the second statement of 20th August 2008 - truthful? Is it true, the contents?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: More or less true. About this other supplement to my testimony, I can't say because I didn't read it through to the end. So I didn't see whether there were any discrepancies in it as there had been in my first testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, at the completion of the -- the interview on the 20th of August, 2008, was the supplemental statement read back to you in your own language?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And after having -- after the statement was read back to you in your own language, did you sign that statement as being a truthful statement of yours?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, if the questions that were asked of you by the members of the Office of the Prosecutor in 2004 and 2008 were asked again here in court, would your responses be the same? As in not the terminology or the language but substance of your statements, would it be the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're getting into areas here because the witnesses has referred to discrepancies, and I know we have the mantra of the 92 ter attestation in this court. But it occurs to me, and it may be of some thing of importance to the Bench, that problems such as this are properly dealt with in terms of his attestation now. He has referred to discrepancies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: He hasn't referred to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, could I ask the witness to take his earphones off for a second. Could you take your earphones off for a second? I understood the witness as follows: That although the proofing statement was read to him, that he had not yet had opportunity to read through in full that statement. I understood this to be the B/C/S translation of this statement, which was taken in English and put on paper in English. And that, therefore, not having read it again, that he was not certain yet whether there were any discrepancies as he found them in his first statement. That's how I understood what he said about discrepancies. If you would agree with me, we could put that to the witness, and then seek his attestation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not trying to split hairs, but the question was: "If the questions that were asked of you by the members of the Office of the Prosecutor 2004, 2008 were asked again here in court, would your responses be the same? As in not the terminology of the language but the substance of your statements, would it be the same?" And it was that, as I called it, the mantra, which is a matter that should be adapted to the circumstances because the witness has referred to the discrepancies and that the first statement was read back to him in English or produced to him in English - not read back but produced to him in English - and he's referred to discrepancies. So if that first statement was read back to him today, the answer to that would be no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course. But I understood that Ms. Mahindaratne took the two statements together to see that the entirety that is the first statement and then as an amended, corrected, clarified, changed, whatever word we use in the second one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps that's the language that should be used as Your Honours' formula. That is really what I'm submitting upon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me try --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... May I?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is nowhere in the Rules that the parties should seek the attestation, so perhaps I will try to do it. Mr. Dzolic, if the same questions were asked as the questions you answered in your statement, would you give the same answers as you gave in 2004 as corrected or amended in your 2008 statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would probably respond in the same way. But as for the corrections I made, I don't know whether there are any fresh errors, whether I have been misunderstood, as I was misunderstood when I gave my statement in 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne -- Apparently, you have not been able to read through in your own language the statement you gave a month ago. Perhaps you could read them during the first break, if there's a copy available, and then report to us if there are any such errors. But from your recollection, as the statement, including the 2008 statement, was read back to you in your own language, would you give the same answers; that is, the answers that you gave in 2004, as corrected, changed, amended in 2008?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before my arrival to today's session, I was shown the amendments to my testimony of 2008; and glancing through it quickly, I observed some things which might be interpreted differently from what I was trying to say in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, is there a recording of the proofing session?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. There is no recording; but what can you done, Mr. President, at this stage until the break, so that we don't lose time, I could move to admit the first statement; and during the break, he could be given an opportunity to examine his second statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it, but please don't misunderstand me, the last thing the Defence would wish to happen is that the first statement would be admitted in into evidence with any risk that the second statement would not be admitted into evidence. That seems to be the whole issue here. So, therefore, what we could do is that you tender the statements. We have an attestation which is not yet fully complete, that, either by having a break now or after the first break, to seek completion of the attestation and then decide on admission. That seems to be the proper course. And I'm not responding on behalf of the Defence; but from what I saw, I have not misunderstood their position as admission of the first statement and not yet an admission of the second statement. You see the problem for the Defence with your solution?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I see that. Can I then move it with Your Honour's first proposal; that is, to take a break now, let the witness examine the second statement, and then proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, the disadvantage is that we might end up with three breaks rather than two, and that is a loss of time. Let me just confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, the Chamber would prefer that you proceed at this moment. We'll finally decide on admission after the first break. Meanwhile, if you would focus on those matters which were not corrected in the second statement, there's hardly any chance that the witness could have been misunderstood in his second statement. At the same time, Mr. Dzolic, we will proceed at this moment. You'll have an opportunity to read through the B/C/S version, the version in your own language of the statement, during the first break. If there are any further comments on your behalf, you can give them after the first break. Is that understood? Yes. Then we should assign numbers to them, then, Ms. Mahindaratne. The first --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can I call up the document, Mr. President, on screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But at least we could ask the witness to identify whether these are the statements. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I call document number 5443, please, Mr. Registrar. That's the statement of 2004.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, you see on your screen a document, and if could you just take a look at it and indicate if this is your statement given in 2004. Then go through each page so that can you take a look at your signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if you could go down, take the English page right down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that if we've seen one of the two of the signatures and the last page, that that would do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, yes, Mr. President. And if we could move to the last page, Mr. Registrar, and in the English version also.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, is that your statement -- is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: No. That's not my signature, what you're showing me now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, we're looking at the witness acknowledgment rather than the interpreter's certification, Ms. Mahindaratne, isn't it? So the last page should be the semi-last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. It's the one before the last page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is my signature now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And do you recognise this statement as a statement you made in 2004?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May it be given a number, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit number P875.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P875 is marked for identification. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. May I call document number 5444, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, do you recognise your signature on the first page there, on the English copy?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we could go, Mr. Registrar, to not the last page, the one before the last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, do you recognise your signature there?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And do you recognise this document as a document you signed on 20th August 2008, the statement you signed?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if the document may be given a P number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P876, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May I -- is this an appropriate time to just read a brief summary of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, under the present circumstances, we should delay that until after the first break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, could we call -- could I have document number 1999, please. And in the meanwhile, Mr. President, if the witness could be given the two statements, the B/C/S versions of it, by Madam Usher, and I will not deal with any controversial matters and the witness will be free to indicate if there is a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since there seems to be no objection, could the copies be begin to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, you have been given hard copies of your two statements. If I could ask you to look at paragraph 27 of your 2008 statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, for the record, that is P876, MFI.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you mean 28 or 27?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Paragraph 27 of your 2008 statement, yes?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yeah. In paragraph 27, you were shown -- you refer to a document that is a report from Mr. Lausic entitled, "The Use of Military Police units of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Croatia." Now, is this the document that you identified by way of paragraph 27?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the report of the chief of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if you could go to page 2 of the B/C/S version and page 4 of the English version; and in the B/C/S version, if the document can be taken right down.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, do you note, under the paragraph 2.5, there is a reference to the address of members of paramilitary formations. Can you just clarify what the term "paramilitary formations" there is referred to? What is paramilitary formations? Are they unknown formations or is it a reference to the enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object and ask for some foundation given that is he not the author of the document. She's asking him to essentially interpret what the author of the document says. As far as I know, this document references the witness, but is not a document of the witness. So I will object until there is more foundation as to how this witness -- whether he participated in the drafting or in another way would know specifically what this refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the background of the witness, as such, he should be familiar what the terms is at the very least, and I think that in the presence of the witness, that objection and the manner it was raised was inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. You may proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, this is a document from the military police administration. Are you familiar with that term used in that paragraph? Can you say who the term "paramilitary formations" there is referred to? I'm not asking you to identify the individuals, but what's the formation?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I don't even know who they're referring to, that's for one. As for the definition for "paramilitary formations," if you want my answer, that would mean an enemy armed formation, which is not part of the regular army. Let's use the term "regular" for practical purposes, so it's an enemy unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... thank you, Mr. Dzolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document was included in the 92 ter submission. I could tender into evidence now or shall I leave so that I don't interfere with Mr. Registrar's numbering since it is already tendered with the 92 ter submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it needs a separate number, I take it, since it is -- I think a decision on admission could be taken, unless there is any objection against that at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour. And for my part, it could be admitted as an exhibit and all documents produced that are admissible can be produced that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The Markac Defence is the same, the same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We have no objection to this document, and I think I notified Ms. Mahindaratne last night of the one document that we do object to, just for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Mahindaratne, no objections against any of the documents; therefore, I leave it to you. We can proceed in two ways, either to ask Mr. Registrar to prepare a list assigning numbers to all of the documents and that you just may refer to them and only seek admission on a separate basis for any document which is not yet on your list.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. Then I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I call document 653, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, while the document comes up, if I could ask you to look at your 2004 statement, paragraph 54. Can you take a look at paragraph 54 of your 2004 statement. And in paragraph 54, you identify a document. You say: "The cooperation between the military police and civilian police was not working very well. On 18th of August, 1995, an order was received from the chief of military police administration," and you give the numbers there, "instructing us to have new meetings with the civilian police, identify the problems, and get things working properly." Now, can you please look at the document on the screen. Is that the order you referred to as having been issued by the chief of military police administration on 18th August 1995? And, in fact, you have given the reference numbers. Your reference numbers reads, "SP 80-01/95-158," and the next number is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Can we have the witness take his earphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you, Mr. Dzolic, take your earphones off for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, just if we're going to take -- show documents to the witness, even though they're military police, I would have a standing objection on foundation purposes that we first see what the witness actually himself knows about the document. From paragraph 354, I couldn't determine whether he referenced it independently, that he received an order on the 18th of August, or that the OTP, in the course of the interview, showed him the document, which he then said, "Yes, this looks like an order that Mr. Lausic issued on 18 August," but it doesn't say in the paragraph whether he has any personal knowledge of the order. I make the submission because it is my understanding that this witness in the normal chain of events wouldn't have received a copy of this order, but would have been passed on tasks from his commander. And, so, if we're going to go through documents, I ask first that we establish a foundation with the witness to see does he recall an order, did he see it at the time, does he know anything about it; and then, if not, then we can see what questions can be posed to the witness based on whatever his answers are. And if he does know, then obviously we can interpret the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, what could be the follow-up questions and whatnot is still to be determined. But, Ms. Mahindaratne, I take it that you would agree that once a document is shown to the witness, to ask him whether he saw it at that time or not. This is not an indication that if he has not seen it at that time, that he could not be asked questions as to the language used, the type of orders issued, the concepts that were at that time formulated. So I'm not -- but I think it is good to know at the beginning whether the witness talks about a document he has seen at a later stage or whether he had seen it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. Now that the witness has already seen the document, I will ask whether he is familiar with this document before he saw it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I take it that you will formulate the question to find out what Mr. Misetic thinks is important.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- yes. Before I ask you again - not at this moment by the way to take off your earphones - I'd like to know, do you speak English and do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't understand it. Just a little bit: How are you? What's your name?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No legal stuff. Yes. Ms. Mahindaratne, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, before we go to the document, you referred to, in paragraph 54 of your statement of 2004, to a document as an order received on 18th of August, 1995, from the chief of military police administration. Now, how did you know that such an order was issued by the chief of military police administration on 18th of August? Was that order conveyed to you? Did you see that order? Did you see a copy of that order?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I think that I've already -- I think that I told the Prosecutors -- the investigators who took my first statement where this was mentioned. I think I told them that I had prepared for this interview. I prepared for it at the military police administration and also at the 4th Corps in the archives, which I had access to, the archives of both the military police and the corps. And that is when I wrote down this number, this reference number, and I told the gentleman who interviewed me when I gave my statement that that was when I saw this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you saw this order for the first time in the archives when you did your own research?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, when I had to familiarize myself and when I prepared for this interview with the investigators of the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And before that, on 18th August or just soon thereafter, was this order conveyed to you, either verbally or in other form, by your commander, Mr. -- Colonel Budimir? I mean not the entirety of the order but were you told, for instance, to cooperate, you know, between military police -- military and civilian police?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. As you know, on the 12th of August, I left Knin. So, as far as the participation in Operation Storm, whether he told me about the order in Split, that I should coordinate my actions with the police in Split, I think that in Split itself we had an excellent cooperation with the civilian police. And I don't even know if it was necessary to have this conversation. But if the commander did relay the order, I would have executed it, together with the Ministry of Interior officials in Split.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, can this document be given a P number and admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a new one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It is not included in the 92 ter submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P877.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against admission? No objections. P877 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, just for the record, in your statement, Mr. Dzolic, you give the reference number 512-119-01-95-5470; whereas, this document, the number is exactly that, but the last four -- last digits are "547" not "5470." Is it possible that you made an error when you added that -- gave that last four digits as "5470"?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I was going to mention that it says here "class, SP 80-01/95, and then a 5 is omitted. So under "class," it says "150"; and, whereas, I have "5470" in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I think what you have is "5470" and the document has "547," Mr. Dzolic. I'm talking about the number below. Do you note that?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I cannot really see the number below that. What I see is "class, SP 80-01/95-150."

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In any event --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness is -- MS. MAHINDARATNE, Sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- apparently looking at a document, and I didn't see him looking at the screen. So, in order to follow what you are suggesting, Ms. Mahindaratne, I think he should look at the screen in the original document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: He is looking, Mr. President. I think he didn't quite follow me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to say this: The class number of the document, here on the monitor, is as the Prosecutor said it or read it. But in the document that I have in front of me, it does not reflect the same class. There is a different class number, and then this is an office number. These are two different numbers. Whether there was some kind of omission when the Prosecution wrote down this number as I dictated it to them, or whether they just merged them together, I don't know what exactly this is all about. But in this document and the document in front of us, the class number is not the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, let me just try to understand what happens at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm referring to, Mr. President, the office number, not the class --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, one second, please. Yes. You now ask a question to the witness. You said: "In your statement ..." What paragraph of the statement, to start with?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Paragraph 54, Mr. President, the paragraph 54 that we were following.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because you started talking about numbers without giving us, if I'm not mistaken, without giving us a clue as to where look in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. I thought you were following.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps, Mr. Dzolic, could you look at paragraph 54 in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we find as the -- what appears to be the office number, being 512-119-01-95-5470. Now, the document you just saw on the screen has an office number, which is almost the same, apart from the last zero which does not appear on the document that was on your screen. Ms. Mahindaratne would like to know whether it nevertheless that you were referring to the same document, although there is a slight difference in the office number, and whether that may have been a mistake, especially the last zero, after "547." Was that a mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is possible that it was a mistake, because I can see now that in every other respect those numbers are the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Date is the same, apparently the subject is the same. So, Ms. Mahindaratne, I think this clarifies the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, another matter is that the handwritten numbers are not, as the class number where apparently the witness focussed on, are not perfectly clear, and there may be a transcribing problem because numbers do not need any translation. I don't think there is any dispute between the parties that the witness was referring to this document. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. President, the last two pages of this document, in fact, was tendered by the Defence as D48, but this document is together. So we -- to keep it as complete as possible, we left those two documents. But for the record, the last two documents - that's page 4 and 5 of the English version and B/C/S page 3 and 4 - in fact, are D48.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dzolic --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could we just move to page 2 of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, when you -- you will see in that section where you have -- where there is a title called "Order," order number 2 instructs: "All commanders of platoons -- VP platoons, companies, and battalions, are to contact immediately the highest ranking HV commander in the area of responsibility and completely implement item number 6 of the UEP order," and reference is given to an order dated 16th August, 1995. Now, you did say -- and, in fact, I will tender -- in fairness, I will tender that document just after this. But you did say that you left Knin on 12th August. Do you recall that if --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: -- pursuant to this order, if company commanders and platoon commanders did, indeed, contact or kept in touch with the most senior ranking HV commander in the area? Are you aware that that, indeed, happened?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I cannot say anything about that. I don't know. I can't recall it. I was not a company commander, in which case I would know what another company commander was doing. I can only speak for my company in Split.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you see any records as the company commander -- or the since you were within the 72nd Military Police Battalion, did you see any records of company commanders or platoon commanders liaising or contacting the senior-most ranking HV officer in the area, pursuant to this order? Did you see any records to indicate that this order was implemented?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I didn't see anything. But as far as I recall, sometime in August, I had a conversation with the officers of the military police in Split -- or, rather, the police in Split to improve our cooperation. But whether that referred to this command, whether my battalion commander ordered me to go and have this conversation based on this order, I don't know. But I suppose that other commanders in the field also had to do this, to carry out this order, both with -- both as received from their commanders and also with their subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar. Can I call document 3350, please. Mr. President, this is just a bar table submission just to keep -- since this order is referred to in the previous order, P877, that we just looked at, I'm just submitting this document from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it is not yet on your list, Ms. Mahindaratne?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number P878.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection against P878. P878 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may I have document P47, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, you will see in a minute a document on your screen, which is an order issued by the chief of military police administration, Mr. Lausic, on 14th August which is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It has been tendered by the Defence, D47.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, see, it is addressed to amongst others the 72nd Military Police Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we could move to page 4 of B/C/S and page -- also 4 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, do you note in paragraph 14 -- I will read it. It says, starts off by saying: "Normalize the command and control structure," and then the military police is ordered in this manner: "In daily operational command, subordinate the commanders of the newly established platoons and companies of the Knin VP to the most senior HV commander in the zone of responsibility and send the daily report to them." And, now, as commander of the -- the Knin military police company, can you explain to Court as to how this particular order was implemented by your company?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Objection as to foundation, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: First and foremost, Mr. Dzolic, can you please tell Court if, in fact, this order was conveyed to you by your superior commander, Colonel Budimir. I am referring to paragraph 14. That particular order, was that conveyed to you by Colonel Budimir? No. I'm not referring to your statement, Mr. Dzolic. You see the document on the screen. Do you note paragraph 14?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, I think --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The paragraph 14 of what? The statement or --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Paragraph 14 of the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, perhaps he can take his earphones off. I don't want to taint his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take your earphones off for a second again, please. Yes, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In fairness to the witness, he should be given an opportunity to see the first page. He has already testified that he left Knin on the 12th. This is a document from the 14th. In order not to confuse him, he should be able to at least see that this is a document that issued two days after he left Knin.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, if would you give clear instructions as to what should be shown on the screen. At this moment, we see the first page of this document. Please ask the questions you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, first and foremost, let me ask you, are you familiar with this document? Do you need time to read the document?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I can read it now, but have I have never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you read it and familiarize yourself, and I will take you to paragraph 14. My question is going to be about paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes. We can go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can we have the next page, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Are you finished, Mr. Dzolic?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question is related to paragraph 14 which reads: "Normalize the command and control structure," and then there is certain other instructions. Then the last sentence starts: "In daily operational command, subordinate the commanders of the newly established platoons and companies of the Knin VP to the most senior HV commander in the zone of responsibility and send the daily report to them."

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question -- of course, you said that on 12th, you left Knin. Are you aware as to if, in fact, there was such an order issued to the Knin military police company?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. You should ask Colonel Budimir, the commander of the 43rd [as interpreted] Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, I think you meant to say 72nd Battalion, isn't it, not 43rd. It is recorded incorrectly as 43rd. Now, my question is: At any stage, do you know if the Knin military company commanders or the platoon commanders, did they send daily reports to the senior -- the most senior HV commander in the zone of responsibility? Are you aware of that order being implemented? That's my question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I think that is asked and answered. He answered that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You're referring to page 28, line 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: 4 to 7, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 4 to 7. Yes. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: He has not answered. My first question was whether there was an order issued to the Knin military police company. Now my second question is whether, in fact, he was aware that daily reports were sent. The first question was about whether this order was issued --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's, let's, let's, let's see. Ms. Mahindaratne, Mr. Dzolic [sic] seeks your testimony in relation to the order in which it is said that the companies of the Knin military police would report or should report to the most senior Croatian army commander in the zone of the responsibility and the daily report to them. First of all, did you know that such an order was issued, that this is the way in which they should report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think I said in my first answer that I'm not familiar with this order. This is an order issued by General Lausic and is addressed to the commander of the battalion. I was subordinate to him. I was only a company commander, and it is my battalion commander who would know about this. The lady is probably asking whether I was aware of the reporting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The first question is that even if it is not directly addressed to you, such an order, in writing, nevertheless, sometimes people are aware of the existence of orders or documents which are not directly addressed to them but they nevertheless have knowledge of it. Were you aware of such an order being issued?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not recall. I don't remember this order. I don't remember this report or these paragraphs which are mentioned in this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, Mr. Dzolic, I want it make it perfectly clear to you that the question is about not whether you remember to have seen this before, but whether you were aware of such an order, even if have you not seen it being issued. If you are not aware, please tell us. If you say, "I've never seen it, but was aware that such an order was issued," please tell us as well. Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's possible that I knew about these parameters, but, Your Honour, I have stated I would tell the truth and nothing but the truth. I don't remember this. I don't know whether I'm supposed to say that I saw this or that I didn't see it. I just don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, again, you're referring to having seen it, and my question was about whether you were aware of such an order issued irrespective of whether you have ever seen it. But have I now well understood you that your testimony is ... [Overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- remember having heard about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's certainly an answer. You have no recollection of any awareness at the time that such an order was issued. Now, the second question is whether you were aware of the commanders of newly establish the platoons and companies of the Knin military police reporting to senior Croatian army commanders, the most senior Croatian army commanders. Are you aware of whether this was done or not? So irrespective of whether you have ever seen orders about it, but was there any direct reporting by the newly established platoon and companies of the military police to the most senior HV commanders? In practice, did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't know about those units on the ground, but I did know that the duty service, in the battalion in Split, sent reports to the military police administration and to the commander in its area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you say "commander," commander of what? Military commander, military police commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The official report was sent. It says here that reports should be sent to the commanders on the ground, but this report was also sent to the commander of the military police unit. It was sent to two addresses. One report was drawn up, and then it was addressed to several addressees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And when you are referring to "commander," in addition to the military police administration, you are referring to the Croatian army command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. The military police administration sent it to the chief of the Main Staff depending on the chain of command and the system. The 72nd Military Police Battalion could only have sent reports to the commander of the Military District, and the ones on the ground could send it to the corps commander or the commander of the brigade who was on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, may I call document 5467, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, you examined this document at the proofing session; and, in fact, you have referred to it in paragraph 28 of your 2008 document. That is P876, MFI. And, in fact, you, having examined this document, you expressed some surprise that the records before the 11th of August was not included. Can you say, generally, what type of activity of the Knin military police is recorded in this book?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: In the duty log-book?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The log-book that you're looking at right now on the screen, yes. Generally, what type of activity of the military police is recorded in this book? You're looking at your statement, Mr. Dzolic. You have not been asked that question. It's a fresh question.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: The duty log contains information on the events which took place in the area of responsibility of the company in question. This is the front page. I don't know what's inside on the next pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I know. I will -- we will go through the next pages. My question is a general question: As the company commander of the Knin military police, you would be familiar with this document, would you not?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, according to your statement -- response just now, would all information received by the shift leaders of the Knin military police and any action taken in relation to such information be recorded in this document, generally?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes, if this log-book was maintained as of the first day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in this -- we will go threw this book, Mr. Dzolic, and I will go through a sample of entries. There are a number of entries here where your company has received information about crimes, such as looting or arson --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Shall we -- I must say my learned friend is trying to drive this witness in -- in her direction and her direction alone. We know he left on the 12th of August. This document begins on the 11th of August. He left this company on the 12th of August, so it's not his company thereafter. I really do think, Your Honour, that proper foundation for the questioning of a witness should be established as to what he actually knows, rather than the conclusions of the advocate. I say that with all respect, but we have to follow this, and we're trying to be absorb what's going into the transcript, all of which is potentially significant. And in our submission, this must be done in a proper way with the witness telling us what he knows and whether it's his document, whether he is familiar with how it was produced, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In fact, if Mr. Kay looked at document, he would see that there are entries related to the witness himself because there are entries on the 11th while the witness was there, and the witness has already responded that he is familiar with this document. In his statement, he has identified the document and the evidence is already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you are familiar with the document, that -- I'm familiar with many documents of which I could -- Let's -- if you say, I'll focus on certain entries, let's go to them, see what the date of these entries is, let's see whether the witness has -- what kind of knowledge he has. One of the problems might be that you often introduce questions, for example, by saying, well, this log-book contains, et cetera, et cetera. Let's lock at it step by step. Let's let you formulate your questions, then we will see it brings us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I raise it because the witness answered: "I don't know what's inside on the next page." "Question: I know we will go through the next pages." So, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I simply know that this witness examined this document in its entirety, and that is why it was not anything improper that I was trying to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, I gave you guidance, Ms. Mahindaratne. Mr. Kay, at that moment, since I didn't criticise you for the reasons why, there was no reason to further explain that. I expected Ms. Mahindaratne to proceed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm planning to go through a number of entries, Mr. President. I know that it is five minutes before the break. Would you prefer to take the break now, and I start on this since it is going to be a -- without reaching the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you start with one or two entries and see how that develops, and then we will have a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. If you could go to page 4, Mr. Registrar, of the B/C/S version; and in the English, it would be 7452. In the English, you would have to go to -- if you click on that arrow, it will give you actually the numbers. Yeah, that's correct. 7452, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dzolic, you were the commander of the Knin company on 11th August, were you not? You left on 12th.

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if we can focus on the entry at -- the third entry, that's at 10.00, 10.00 a.m. There is an entry where an information come from the 40th Engineers Company to the shift leader, and the incident relates to a shooting and arson in Kovacic hamlet. And pursuant to that information, Cobra 40 - that is patrol - is sent, and it says "report attached." Now, since you were the company commander at the time, do you recall this incident where there was shooting and arson from the Kovacic hamlet reported to the military police?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I don't recall, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, this says that there is a report attached. Do you know where reports that were raised by the Knin military police were sent to or to what it's attached?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honour. But as I can see, there is an obvious mistake in the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we proceed, we never discuss what should be the translation or is not the translation in the presence of the witness. Mr. Dzolic, could you please take your earphones off for a second. Yes, Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: As I can see in the English version, it is written "report attached." But in the original version which I have in front of me, it is written that "report is in the order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Because it is written in original "izvjesce," that is "report"; "u," that is "in"; and it is not written "prilog," which will be "attachment," but it is written "nalog" which is "order." So it could be kind of confusion in that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This seems to me a perfect moment to have a break, so that the parties could discuss the matter during the break, seek further advice as to whether this is a mistake, because your question apparently was based on "attachments," at least part of your question. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: While the witness has earphones off and before taking the break, I do want to note that I have already sent a e-mail to Mr. Nilsson and Mr. Monkhouse. But I want to put it on the record that I believe that at page 31, lines 18-21, there was a translation error, and we would like to have that checked or put to the witness again while he is here, however the Trial Chamber prefers to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you sent it also to Ms. Mahindaratne?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I did, and I copied all counsel on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was not in your brief report. So we have quite some work to be done during the break. I take it, Ms. Mahindaratne, if there was an error in translation, that you will find a solution either to have it checked or you put it again to the witness in order to clarify the issue, which I'm not aware of yet. Then we'll ask the witness to put his earphones on again. Mr. Dzolic, we discussed potential translation errors, and we don't want you to be a victim of it. It will be all be sorted out during the break. You, however, are invited to check the version you can read of your 2008 statement and see whether there's anything in there which you'd like to further correct or amend or whatever there is. Do you think 25 minutes would be enough to read through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope it will be enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break until five manipulates to 11.00, and we'd like to hear from you then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, could I first ask you whether you had an opportunity to read in your own language your 2008 statement and whether there's any need to hear further comments?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did have an opportunity to see the 2008 statement, and I do need to add a few things after I've briefly gone through this statement. What I'd like to say in paragraph 3, where paragraph 5 is referred to, it says here: "I would like to add that we received orders from the Military District command." To clarify, I would like to say that this was the command of the battalion of the military police and not -- I wasn't speaking for myself. I just want it make sure that it's understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... let me just wait. Yes, now I hear myself again. You said paragraph 3, in relation to paragraph 5 of your 2004 statement, you said you'd like to add that you received orders from the Military District Command Split and also from the military police administration. You would like to add the reference to the battalion, in relation to orders you received from the military police administration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps I'll do it in such a way: You said you'd like to make a clear reference that it was orders you received from the battalion. Where you there referring to the military police battalion, as we find in paragraph 5 of your 2004 statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is on the record. Your next point, Mr. Dzolic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 4, where reference is made to paragraph 7, discussing the reporting system --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- where it says that the reports were compiled, based on work orders and reports by patrols of the military police, and not unit commanders. This could be a platoon commander or a company commander, but here it is actually based on the check-points. And based on those reports, the duty service of the battalion or the company would compile a report that would be sent to the duty service of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, did I correctly understand you that the reports were drafted by the patrols, which could be under a platoon commander or a company commander, but it was the information from the check-points that was the basis for it, and that it was sent to the duty service to finally compile the report that would be sent to the duty service of the battalion? Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's, then, on the record as well. Next point, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 5, where reference is made to paragraph 10, it says here that I said I would like to add that the military courts could deal with crimes. What I could like here to be written was not could deal but they dealt with crimes, or, rather, criminal offences committed by members of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that would be criminal offences of any seriousness, all of them, from the most serious to less serious ones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to clarify something here. Military courts dealt with serious crimes, such as murder, looting, robbery, and similar; and as for minor offences, such as disciplinary offences, they would be dealt with by disciplinary courts, in keeping with the rules on military discipline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you said military courts could not only deal with these crimes but they actually dealt with those crimes. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your next point, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 16, where reference is made to paragraph 38, where it says that the main task of the military police was to escort or to bring in perpetrators and investigate crimes committed by members of the army. If a local commander, military commander, was informed that a crime was committed, his duty was to report this to the military police. The word "local" here is very general, so I would like to -- I would like there to be written instead "to the immediate superior." So, in other words, if there were ten superiors to the perpetrator, then they would all have had to react; and the commander, the immediate commander, would have to report this to the platoon commander. If his immediate superior was a platoon commander, then he would have to report it to the company commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The word "local" appears twice. Could you guide me exactly to the line where you would like to make --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If I can point out, in the translation, it was translated as: "So, in other words, if there were ten superiors to the perpetrator," and I think what the translation should have been is if the commander, if it was a squad, the "squad commander" is what he said in Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, Mr. Misetic, it appears to be a rather technical issue; but, in general, the correct translation should not be presented to the Chamber when the witness is listening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay. I apologise. But just the ten superiors is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. There seems to be confusion. Could you tell me exactly is it the line somewhere in the middle of the paragraph or at the end? In the middle it says: "If it was reported to a local military commander that a crime was committed." And at the end of this paragraph, we read: "The local commander could discipline his soldiers himself if it was a minor breach." I got the impression that you wanted to refer to the middle of the paragraph. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. But it should also be corrected in the next sentence because wherever mention is made of "local commander," instead, it should be the "immediate superior."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The "immediate superior" is replacing, twice, the reference to the "local commander." Your next point, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 18, where reference is made to paragraph 45, where it says: "We went to several locations and saw some houses and structures burning." In other words, a military police patrol went to several locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you say "we," you are referring to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A military police patrol. I just wanted to be clear. I was not the one who went and visited those several locations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you said "military police patrols" went to several locations and saw some houses. That's on the record. Next point, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the same paragraph, where it says I was "sent" by Cermak to see the commanders of the 142nd Brigade, I would like, instead, that it reads that he "proposed" or "recommended," because where it -- when it says "sent," it could imply that he ordered me, but, in fact, he couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is clear. Your next point, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 25, where the rules governing the structures and operation of the military police are discussed. When I say that this is confirmed-- my statement confirms this, I mean the explanation of paragraphs Article 8 and 9, where it clearly says that the military police administration orders the units of the military police; whereas, the commander of the Military District issues orders that relate to daily operational tasks that the police had to carry out in the field. And these daily operational tasks would entail guarding of special buildings, persons, personalities, and areas, and providing security for convoys of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that replaces or is in addition to what you called the regular military police tasks? Is that a clarification of what you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. It says here "regular military police tasks"; instead, it should read "daily operational tasks."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Next point, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 26, referring to an order by Mate Lausic, regarding the subordination of the military police to the most senior HV commander in the respective zone of responsibility, I would like the "daily activities" to be replaced by "daily operational tasks."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it reads: "For the daily operational tasks of the 72nd Military Police Battalion ..." That's on the record. Next point, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I read this briefly, I don't think I have any more objections to this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now we come back to a question which was earlier put to you, whether you would answer the questions in a similar way as you did when giving these statements. Would you give the same answer - that is to say, the answers that you gave in 2004 - as corrected, explained, changed in your 2008 statement, taking into consideration the further explanations and the further amendments to that statement, as you've just given it to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm addressing the parties, especially Defence. It seems that the attestation is now complete. If you would disagree, please tell the Court. I hear of no disagreement, which means that P875 and P876 are admitted in into evidence. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you resolved the translation issue that apparently --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. In fact, Mr. Mikulicic was correct. There was a translation error there, and it says here that "the report is attached," but it should read, in fact, that "an order has been issued requesting a report."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's on the record now as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Dzolic, we were looking at the entry on the document on your screen - if could you lock at it - at 1000 hours, where there's information about shooting and arson, and a military police patrol is sent. There's a note there that an order has been issued requesting a report. Now, this was a time when you were the commander of the -- this company. Can you tell Court who in such circumstances would issue an order to a patrol, to submit a report?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you note the entry there at 10.00 in the morning where --

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... there's a note in relation to that information about shooting and arson. A patrol is sent, and there's a note there that an order has been issued requesting a report. Now, you were the commander of the -- this company on the 11th. Now, can you tell Court who in these circumstances could issue an order to the patrol to submit a report on this incident?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the way I interpret this log-book of the duty service -- or, rather, a log-book of events that occurred in the area of responsibility, I think it is clear here who -- from whom a report was received that an event occurred or that an act was committed and then the duty service that sends a patrol to investigate in the field. And the report in an order would mean each patrol had a daily order where they were ordered what they're are to carry out on that day, and they would report on their work by filling out this order form. And if anything was discovered or observed, then this patrol would have the responsibility to also draft an additional note on the event, about the event; and then submit it to the duty service, so that then it could be reported through the chain of command, this event could be reported through the chain of command. I don't know if this clarifies the question that was put to me by the Prosecutor. So, in other words, this was there duty. There is no special order for them to compile a report. The patrol would have to draft a report and fill out this work order that they have with them; and once they did that, it would be sent to the duty service. And if the perpetrator was caught, he would be taken to the duty service, which would then take it over upon themselves to refer this person for further criminal processing to the crime police; and a member of the military police patrol would then draft his own report on the event. This was standard procedure; and from what I can see and the way I interpret this, I think it is clear in itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And those reports that the patrols would submit, would they be archived somewhere?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: They were archived in the unit, at the headquarters of the unit. So, if there was a patrol, a company patrol, then it would be archived in the company. If it was a company that was attached as a unit to a battalion, in this case, a Split battalion, and later on when it was transferred to Knin, the 72nd Battalion, then this would have been archived at the seat of the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in this -- in relation to this entry, there is an record that a patrol, military police, was sent out. Now, when information was received by the shift leader of the military police company, under what circumstances would a military police patrol be sent? What I'm asking you is to focus on the fact whether -- would the military police patrol be sent in realities to any incident reported, or would it have to fall within the purview of the military police activity? And, for instance, would military police still be sent if, in fact, the crime or incident reported involved exclusively civilians?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: A military police patrol -- or, rather, the military police, in keeping with their authorisation, were only able to take action vis-a-vis members of the Croatian army. If a duty service, by some chance, were to receive a report on an incident committed by a civilian or involving a civilian, then the duty service would get in touch with the duty service of the civilian police and refer the information or forward the information to them. And it was their duty or their responsibility, just as it was ours, to go to the crime scene and process that perpetrator if it was a civilian perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if, in fact, the person who received the information contacted civilian police, as you just stated, would that fact be recorded in this log-book also, the fact that MUP has been contacted or civilian police has been contacted?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: It would.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, moving down on that same page, at 1710 hours, there is -- there's information received from Golubic by a military police patrol, Mosor 91.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: M-o-s-o-r, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And it records that the removal of bodies and medical services are required, and then: "Military police has informed Knin garrison command -- sorry, Knin garrison informed, but I could not get a doctor on the phone." And my question to you is: Why was the Knin garrison informed in relation to these type of matters?

utterances.speaker: BOSKO DZOLIC
utterances.text: Why? Well, you would need to ask the duty service in this particular case. I don't know what their orders were, what their instructions were, regarding the clearing up of the field. But I think that they did so because there was a doctor there who was -- whose duty it was to sanitize the terrain, and I think that I mentioned that this was normally down by the civilian police. I think this was in my statement. However, this particular event involved a military installation; in other words, the Military District doctor was probably supposed to get in touch with his technical service, take them to the crime scene or the spot, and carry out the sanitation of the terrain. That is why I think they were looking for a doctor at the Military District in Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm looking -- if he could take his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you take your earphones off, Mr. Dzolic?
